qti-assessment-test.title: SE University - ASCE 7-22 Wind/Tornado Loads & ACI 318-19 Shear Lug Connections PDH (Demo)

qti-assessment-item.title: Determine Risk Category III and IV tornado-load applicability and updated Kz velocity pressure exposure coefficients under ASCE 7-22 Chapters 26 through 32.

qti-item-body.p: Objective (OBJ_1): Determine Risk Category III and IV tornado-load applicability and updated Kz velocity pressure exposure coefficients under ASCE 7-22 Chapters 26 through 32.

qti-choice-interaction.qti-prompt: Under ASCE/SEI 7-22 Chapter 32, which project requires a mandatory Tornado Load evaluation in addition to Chapters 27-30 wind design?
qti-choice-interaction.qti-simple-choice: A Risk Category II suburban warehouse located in Oklahoma City
A Risk Category IV acute-care hospital or Risk Category III public high school located within the ASCE 7-22 Tornado-Prone Region
A Risk Category I agricultural storage barn in Kansas
Any single-family detached residence nationwide regardless of Risk Category

qti-content-body.p: Diagnostic rationale: ASCE 7-22 Chapter 32 (Section 32.1.1) applies strictly to Risk Category III and IV structures in the Tornado-Prone Region, not Risk Category II.
Verified: Section 32.1.1 mandates Chapter 32 tornado load determination for Risk Category III and IV buildings located in the Tornado-Prone Region.
Diagnostic rationale: Risk Category I structures are excluded from Chapter 32 tornado design.
Diagnostic rationale: Residential Risk Category II structures are outside the scope of mandatory ASCE 7-22 Chapter 32 provisions.

qti-assessment-item.title: Calculate concrete bearing strength and concrete breakout capacity for welded steel base-plate shear lugs under ACI 318-19 Section 17.11.

qti-item-body.p: Objective (OBJ_2): Calculate concrete bearing strength and concrete breakout capacity for welded steel base-plate shear lugs under ACI 318-19 Section 17.11.

qti-choice-interaction.qti-prompt: When calculating the effective concrete bearing area (Abrg) of a welded steel shear lug beneath a 2-inch non-shrink grout pad under ACI 318-19 Section 17.11.2, which portion of the lug depth contributes to bearing resistance?
qti-choice-interaction.qti-simple-choice: The entire total depth of the shear lug measured from the underside of the steel base plate, including the 2-inch grout layer
Only the embedded portion of the shear lug projecting into the structural concrete foundation below the grout bed (excluding grout thickness)
Twice the base-plate plan area regardless of lug embedment depth
Zero concrete bearing check is required if anchor rods are ASTM F1554 Grade 55

qti-content-body.p: Diagnostic rationale: ACI 318-19 Section 17.11.2 excludes the grout bed thickness from effective bearing area while still accounting for the grout lever arm in lug bending.

Verified: Effective bearing area Abrg includes only the projected lug area bearing directly against structural concrete below the grout pad, though grout thickness increases bending moment on the lug-to-base-plate weld.
Diagnostic rationale: Base-plate plan area governs vertical axial bearing, not horizontal shear-lug face bearing.
Diagnostic rationale: Anchor rod grade does not waive ACI 318-19 Section 17.11 bearing and concrete breakout checks on a shear lug.

qti-assessment-item.title: Verify load-distribution compatibility so cast-in anchor bolts and welded shear lugs are not erroneously summed directly in column base shear transfer.

qti-item-body.p: Objective (OBJ_3): Verify load-distribution compatibility so cast-in anchor bolts and welded shear lugs are not erroneously summed directly in column base shear transfer.

qti-choice-interaction.qti-prompt: Why do ACI 318-19 Section 17.11.1 and AISC Design Guide 1 prohibit directly adding standard-oversized-hole anchor-rod shear strength to welded shear-lug shear capacity at a column base?
qti-choice-interaction.qti-simple-choice: Deformation incompatibility: the stiff grouted shear lug engages and triggers concrete breakout before the base plate slips far enough across oversized holes to engage unweighted anchor rods
Steel anchor rods dissolve chemically when placed within 12 inches of a welded shear lug
ASCE 7-22 bans anchor rods on any column subjected to wind uplift
Welded shear lugs resist only tension uplift and carry zero horizontal shear

qti-content-body.p: Verified: Base-plate holes per AISC Table 14-2 are significantly oversized; concrete breakout at the stiff shear lug occurs at tiny displacements long before anchor rods bear in shear.
Diagnostic rationale: No chemical incompatibility exists between carbon/alloy steel anchor rods and structural steel shear lugs.
Diagnostic rationale: Anchor rods remain essential for uplift tension and erection stability.
Diagnostic rationale: Shear lugs specifically transfer horizontal base shear into the concrete pedestal, never tension uplift.

qti-item-body.p: Objective (OBJ_2): Calculate concrete bearing strength and concrete breakout capacity for welded steel base-plate shear lugs under ACI 318-19 Section 17.11.

qti-choice-interaction.qti-prompt: A shear lug transfers horizontal shear toward a nearby free edge of a concrete pier. In addition to lug bearing, plate bending, and base-plate weld sizing, which concrete failure limit state must be checked under ACI 318-19 Section 17.11.3?
qti-choice-interaction.qti-simple-choice: Concrete shear breakout (Vcbg) of the pier edge in front of the shear lug, accounting for axial anchor tension effects where applicable
Timber grain crushing perpendicular to load
Soil liquefaction only, omitting pedestal concrete checks
Punching shear of an elevated post-tensioned roof slab

qti-content-body.p: Verified: ACI 318-19 Section 17.11.3 requires checking concrete breakout strength in shear toward free edges (and checking whether anchor tension cracks the breakout prism).
Diagnostic rationale: Timber bearing provisions do not apply to reinforced concrete pedestals.
Diagnostic rationale: Geotechnical checks never replace structural concrete pedestal breakout design.
Diagnostic rationale: Two-way slab punching shear is distinct from pedestal edge shear breakout in front of a shear lug.
